CHAPTER I

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definitions

heading: Article 1
translated_text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency.
5. Social Service, Women Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning, hereinafter referred to as the Service, is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Implementation of Women and Child Protection.
6. Women Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.
8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as the Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.
9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
10. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
13. Children's Forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
14. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
15. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender-sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence.
25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
29. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from generation to generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns.

Obligations of the Community

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Obligations Regarding the Protection of Women

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women is obliged to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of women's rights in the household.

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

1. The Regent is responsible for the implementation of Gender Mainstreaming in the Region.
2. The responsibility of the Regent as referred to in paragraph (1) may be delegated to the Vice Regent.

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

In implementing Gender Mainstreaming in the region, the Regent appoints the Regional Apparatus in charge of Women's Empowerment as the coordinator for the implementation of Gender Mainstreaming.

heading: Part Three

Part Three

Formation of Gender Mainstreaming Working Group

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

1. In an effort to accelerate the institutionalization of Gender Mainstreaming in all Regional Apparatus, a Gender Mainstreaming Working Group is formed.
2. The Gender Mainstreaming Working Group as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. chairperson: Head of Bapppeda;
b. secretary: Head of the Regional Apparatus in charge of Women's Empowerment; and c. members: all heads/leaders of Regional Apparatus.
3. The formation of the Gender Mainstreaming working group as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

heading: Article 16
Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

1. The technical team as referred to in Article 16 letter j consists of officials who understand gender-responsive budget analysis.
2. The Regional Gender Mainstreaming regional action plan as referred to in Article 16 letter k contains:
a. gender mainstreaming in regional legislation;
b. gender mainstreaming in the regional development cycle;
c. strengthening of Gender Mainstreaming institutions in the region; and
d. strengthening community participation in the region

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

General

heading: Article 26
Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. The implementation of UPTD PPA services is integrative, which is carried out under one roof or networked to provide optimal services to women and children who experience problems.
2. In the event that the implementation of UPTDPPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out under one roof, UPTD PPA is responsible for carrying out the entire process in one unit to provide the services needed by women and children who experience problems.
3. In the event that the implementation of UPTDPPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a network, UPTD PPA is responsible for the entire referral process for services needed by women and children who experience problems.
4. Every element within the UPTDPPA environment in carrying out its duties must apply the principles of coordination, integration, synchronization, accountability and openness, both within the UPTDPPA environment, as well as in relations between Regional Apparatuses, related agencies, and community elements.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

Further provisions regarding the organization and working procedures of UPTDPPA as referred to in Article 26 and Article 27 shall be stipulated by Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Complaint Services

heading: Article 29
Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/orc. by letter.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Health Rehabilitation

heading: Article 31
Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Social Rehabilitation

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women and children who experience social dysfunction due to criminal and/or civil problems to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services for:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. In implementing services as referred to in paragraph (2), UPTD PPA may cooperate with women crisis centres and/or existing social community organizations.

heading: Article 33
Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

1. The provision of safe houses as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) letter b may be provided by the Regional Government for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include:
a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

1. Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) letter c aims at psychological recovery.
2. Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
3. Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.

heading: Paragraph 5
translated_text:
Paragraph 5

Assistance

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. Accompaniment services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter d are carried out for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
2. In providing accompaniment services as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A may cooperate with persons or institutions that have expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy.

heading: Paragraph 6
translated_text:
Paragraph 6

Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

heading: Article 37
Paragraph 7
translated_text:
Paragraph 7

Repatriation and Social Reintegration

heading: Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

1. Repatriation as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter f is intended to return women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems to their place of origin.
2. Repatriation of women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

heading: Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

1. Social reintegration as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) is carried out in order to reunite women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to enable women and children as victims to resume their social life and have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

heading: Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

Repatriation and social reintegration of women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems as referred to in Article 38 and Article 39 are implemented by UPTDPPA in accordance with laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

FAMILY QUALITY IMPROVEMENT

Article 41

1. In order to improve family quality, the Regional Government is responsible for:
a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and Children's rights;
b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and Children's rights; and c. strengthening and developing family quality improvement service provider institutions in the Region.
2. The responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

heading: Article 42
translated_text:
Article 42

Efforts to improve family quality as referred to in Article 41 paragraph (1) letter a include:
a. guidance;
b. counseling; and
c. supervision.

heading: Article 43
Article 44
Article 45
translated_text:
Article 45

Supervision as referred to in Article 42 letter c includes:
a. evaluating data on toddler growth and development;
b. evaluating post-marriage data.

heading: Article 46
Article 47
translated_text:
Article 47

Communication, information and education as referred to in Article 46 letter a constitute communication activities to increase knowledge and improve the attitudes and behavior of families and communities in population and family planning Programs.

heading: Article 48
translated_text:
Article 48

1. Agencies and private parties that provide public services must provide lactation rooms.
2. Lactation rooms as referred to in paragraph (1) are proper and adequate rooms.
3. Agency heads who do not provide lactation rooms as referred to in paragraph (1) are subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. written reprimand; and/or
b. employment sanctions based on the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
4. Private parties who do not provide lactation rooms as referred to in paragraph (2) are subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. written warning;
b. limitation of business activities;
c. suspension of business activities;
d. administrative fines; and/or
e. revocation of permits.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

GENDER AND CHILD DATA SYSTEM

Part One

General

heading: Article 49
translated_text:
Article 49

1. In order to prepare planning, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation, as well as policy making for gender-responsive and child-friendly development, the regional government organizes a gender and child data system.
2. To organize a gender and child data system, accurate and accountable disaggregated data is required.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Implementation of Gender and Child Data System

heading: Article 50
translated_text:
Article 50

1. In implementing the gender and child data system in the region as referred to in Article 49, the Regent establishes a working group for gender and child disaggregated data.
2. The establishment of the gender and child disaggregated data working group as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

heading: Article 51
CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

FULFILLMENT OF CHILDREN'S RIGHTS

Part One

General

heading: Article 52
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of Birth Registration and Child Identity

heading: Article 53
translated_text:
Article 53

1. The Regional Government is obliged to organize the registration of Children's births with the issuance of birth certificates.
2. Birth certificates as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be organized free of charge.

heading: Article 54
translated_text:
Article 54

1. To encourage increased data collection, protection and public services and to realize the best interests of children, every child under the age of 17 years must have a child identity card.
2. Child identity cards shall be issued by the Regional Apparatus responsible for population and civil registration.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of education

heading: Article 55
translated_text:
Article 55

The Regional Government guarantees the implementation of compulsory education programs for Children in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 56
translated_text:
Article 56

1. Every organizer of an education unit is obliged to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
2. Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
3. In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence shall be provided with formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the education unit and coordinated with the Women and Child Empowerment Unit

heading: Article 57
translated_text:
Article 57

1. Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
2. Every Child has the right to receive Protection in education units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

heading: Article 58
translated_text:
Article 58

1. Children with disabilities and Children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal education services, including inclusive education programs.
2. The regional government provides educators for inclusive education in every education unit.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of Health and Social

heading: Article 59
Article 60
Article 61
Article 62
translated_text:
Article 62

1. Curative efforts for basic health services as referred to in Article 59 paragraph (2) letter a are aimed at preventing disease from becoming more severe through treatment.
2. Treatment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented free of charge for children from underprivileged families.

heading: Article 63
translated_text:
Article 63

1. Rehabilitative efforts for basic health services as referred to in Article 59 paragraph (2) letter a are aimed at maintaining and restoring conditions after illness.
2. Rehabilitative efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through periodic health examinations.

heading: Article 64
Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of Employment

heading: Article 65
translated_text:
Article 65

The Regional Government conducts periodic supervision of every person/entity that employs Children in the effort to Protect child workers.

heading: Article 66
translated_text:
Article 66

1. Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving Children in the worst forms of work.
2. The worst forms of work referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. all work in the form of slavery or the like;
b. all work that utilizes, provides, or offers Children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances, or gambling;
c. all work that utilizes, provides, or involves Children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropics, and other addictive substances; and/or
d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of Children.

heading: Part Six
translated_text:
Part Six

Children's Forum

heading: Article 67
translated_text:
Article 67

1. In organizing the fulfillment of children's rights to express opinions and participate, the Regional Government facilitates the establishment of a Children's Forum.
2. The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes a representation of Children in the Region.
3. The representation as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of the geographical domicile of Children, components of Children's socio-cultural groups and Children's educational background.
4. The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) may be established at the Regional, Sub-district and Nagari levels.
5. In every formulation of policies related to Children, the Regional Government is obliged to consider and accommodate the opinions of Children submitted through the Children's Forum.
6. The establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

CHILD-FRIENDLY REGENCY

Article 68

1. In the framework of fulfilling Children's rights in an integrated, systematic and sustainable manner, the Regional Government establishes a policy for the Development of CFC.
2. The policy for the Development of CFC as referred to in paragraph (1) contains:
a. the concept of CFC concerning objectives, strategies and roles of related parties;
b. Children's rights; and
c. the approach to CFC development.

heading: Article 69
Article 70
Article 71
translated_text:
Article 71

In carrying out its duties, the CFC Task Force as referred to in Article 70 paragraph (1) may coordinate and cooperate with the UPTD PPA and/or other institutions that provide Protection and Child services.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. the formulation of policies and regulations used as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection;
b. technical guidance and training, comprising:
1\. providing training for government officials and law enforcers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2\. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3\. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4\. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5\. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
3. The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
4. The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.
5. Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 73

Financing for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection activities is sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and other sources that are lawful and non-binding

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 74

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation shall be stipulated no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 75
translated_text:
Article 75

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Dharmasraya Regency.

Article 9

Paragraph(1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) What is meant by Ninik Mamak is a man from a clan who is respected and becomes "tampek baiyo dan bamolah" (deliberates) even though still young. In this case it includes the head of lineage mamak and the head of inheritance mamak in the clan, whether he is an ulama, intellectual, community leader, laborer, farmer or even an official.

What is meant by Alim ulama is a leader of the Minangkabau community in religious matters, namely a person who is considered learned. A learned person is a person who has extensive knowledge and has faith, whose existence in society is very much needed. This is expressed in Minangkabau custom adat basandi syarak, syarak basandi kitabullah. The existence of alim ulama in Minangkabau society covers Islamic religion/sharia.

What is meant by Cadiak Pandai is a community leader who has extensive knowledge and insight as well as thinking that can find a way out of every problem being faced by Minangkabau society. Cadiak pandai is a collection of intelligent people, knowledgeable, clever, intellectuals, and people who are quick to understand, skilled at finding problem solutions and have broad thinking.

What is meant by Bundo Kanduang is a term for the group of women in Minangkabau, bundo means mother and kanduang means true. Bundo kanduang means, a true mother who has maternal and leadership qualities.

Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear

Article 33

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by Counselor is a trained officer who conducts counseling, namely the provision of assistance by an expert/trained person in such a way that the psychological understanding and ability of the victim increases in solving the problems faced.

Letter b What is meant by Psychologist is a person who has the ability to carry out psychological recovery for women and children victims of violence.

Letter c What is meant by Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession whose duty is to handle mental disorder problems.

heading: Article 58
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF DHARMASRAYA REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 58

Paragraph (1) What is meant by children with special needs are children who experience limitations/disabilities whether physical, mental-intellectual, social, or emotional that significantly affect their growth and development process compared to other children of the same age.

What is meant by formal education is systematic, structured, tiered activities starting from elementary school to higher education and its equivalent, including academically and generally oriented study activities, specialization programs, and professional training conducted on a continuous basis.

What is meant by non-formal education is an educational pathway outside formal education that can be implemented in a structured and tiered manner.

What is meant by informal education is the pathway of family education (tutoring, home schooling, private) and environment. Education is organized by providing examples, building willingness, and developing the creativity of students in the learning process.

What is meant by inclusive education is an educational service system that includes children with special needs learning together with their peers in regular schools closest to their place of residence.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently Clear

heading: Article 59
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF DHARMASRAYA REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 59

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by promotive efforts is to improve so that health status becomes increasingly improved, for example providing early breastfeeding initiation (EBI) and exclusive breastfeeding which can help increase immunity to disease because of colostrum and nutrients contained in breast milk, so that children are not easily affected by disease.

What is meant by preventive efforts is to prevent from contracting disease or to keep healthy people healthy, for example washing hands before eating and after defecating will prevent the occurrence of diarrhea.

What is meant by curative efforts is the process of curing a person from a state of physical and psychological illness.

What is meant by rehabilitative efforts is the process of maintaining so that a person who has recovered (not yet 100% recovered) returns to being fit as before. Letter b Sufficiently clear Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear
